title: Learning: Already Inside
text: A call arrives from an address inside the cluster. Later, a request reaches the user service asking for an export of every account.
held: Being inside the network earned nothing: the caller had an identity, and the identity had the right.

cards.label: Block the call
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: identity
fields.check: Ask the caller for its identity

intrusion.detail: No certificate. Only an inside address.
intrusion.why: An inside address is where an intruder is standing after the first breach. Zero trust means position earns nothing.
intrusion.reveal: The call came from an inside address with no identity at all.

temptations.label: Allow it: the network policy only lets cluster pods reach you
temptations.why: Then the network policy is doing your authentication, and any pod in the cluster passes it, including a compromised one.

cards.label: Refuse the request
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: caller's role
fields.check: Check what this caller's role allows

intrusion.detail: The caller is frontend. Frontend may read one account at a time, not export them all.
intrusion.why: A real, verified frontend asking for every account is what a compromised frontend looks like.
intrusion.reveal: The export request came from the frontend service, which is not allowed to export.

teaches: Network position is not identity. Every call is authenticated, wherever it comes from.
Least privilege limits what a compromised but genuine service can do.
